chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the squeezer dog (greyhound). He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you touch it, wash your hand.'

key_terms.الْكَلْبِ السَّلُوقِيِّ: The greyhound or squeezer dog, a specific breed mentioned in hadith with distinct rulings.
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْ يَدَكَ: So wash your hand (indicating the required act of purification).
key_terms.مَسِسْتَهُ: You touched it (referring to the dog).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing hands after touching a greyhound dog in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific juristic distinction made by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the 'kalb al-salooqi' (greyhound), a breed often kept for hunting and thus considered more noble than the common stray dog. The ruling of washing the hand upon touch reflects the Shia principle of 'alaqah' (adhesion) of impurity to the surface, distinguishing it from the seven-wash requirement for the saliva of other dogs, thereby illustrating the nuanced approach to ritual purity in fiqh.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the greyhound dog. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you touch it, so wash your hand’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ibn Mahbub from al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the dog from al-Saluqiy (name of a place in Yemen). He (the Imam) said, ‘If you touch it you must then wash your hands.’”
